parts.article:
Images and Places
 
A new research method uses photography to try to explain why people form an attachment to certain places
 
A Human beings naturally become attached to places they visit or inhabit and these emotional attachments have become increasingly important in research on recreation sites and activities. Research into this phenomenon is called 'sense-of-place research'. This research has employed a variety of approaches to gauge people's feelings toward a place, including surveys and personal interviews, but so far has not used photo-based methods. However, Visitor Employed Photography (VEP), used to capture visitor perceptions of landscape and recreational quality, represents a potential innovation in sense-of-place research.
 
B A 'place' is a setting that we give meaning to based on the personal experiences, relationships and feelings we associate with it. A crucial distinction that needs to be made is between the more subjective concept of attachment and the symbolic 'meanings' or labels we use to describe the type of place a setting represents. Is, for example, a multiple-use forest area a wilderness? A playground? A workplace? Symbolic meanings are important in that they form the basis of our attachment to a place: we attribute meaning to our settings, and in turn become attached to the meanings (Stedman, 2003). All settings can have multiple meanings depending on how we encounter them. Some researchers suggest that, because meaning emerges through individual experience, for example 'my camping trip', place meanings are completely individualistic: a given setting such as a park will contain as many different meanings as there are people using the setting (Meinig, 1979). Others, however, (e.g. Greider & Garkovich, 1994) assert that meanings are based on social categories and therefore are shared by others within these categories. For example, farmers share certain meanings for a plot of land that are distinct from those of real-estate developers or hunters.
 
C Clearly, place attachment is built through familiarity with a place over a period of months or even years. Relph (1976) describes sense-of-place attachment as the steady accumulation of events within a setting; this creates 'home places'. According to this view, those who have participated fully in the life of the home or community, or have accumulated a series of everyday events in a setting, will have the strongest attachment to it. Extended residence in a place tends to make us feel toward it almost as a living thing, affecting our emotions in the same way as a family would (Ryden, 1993). However, Tuan (1977) notes that a sense of place may also develop quite rapidly in 'chosen places', where dramatic landscapes and intense experiences can lead to an immediate attachment. Indeed, many settings, especially those that attract visitors, may simultaneously exist as home places and chosen places.
 
D Clearly we are dealing with a complex phenomenon and photo-based research methods may help us to understand it better. In VEP, tourists are asked to take photographs. This technique has primarily been used to assess the perceptions of visitors to parks and recreation places. Haywood (1990) describes several benefits of VEP. Photography is an enjoyable, familiar activity to tourists which helps to sharpen observation and identify specific locations that are important. It can give clearer ideas on elements that are liked or disliked and also facilitates comparisons between places.
 
E However, several methodological issues need to be taken into account. First, who should take the photographs? VEP research typically involves visitors or tourists but, when applied to questions of attachment to a community, this approach has potential pitfalls. Chenoweth (1984) notes that research subjects may take photos that represent only a part of their entire recreational experience. This tendency probably relates to unfamiliarity with the setting. For example, when researchers assign the task of photographing a travel route with which respondents are not familiar, participants may save too many pictures and then use them all up at the end of their visit, even if there is no suitable material. Markwell (1997) noted an opposite tendency in his study of pictures taken on a nature tour: beginnings of excursions were over-represented, due perhaps to the initial novelty of the trip. Furthermore, Haywood (1990) suggests that compressing the photo-taking period into a single day (as he did in his work) may result in an over-representation of tourist icons rather than ordinary places. In contrast, Yamashita (2002), when focusing on local residents' perceptions of the qualities of the water around them, noted that residents may have more difficulty expressing visual appeal than visitors, precisely because they are insiders and less conscious of aesthetic qualities. When addressing complex attachment to landscape, we would expect, however, that familiarity ought to increase the validity of the items selected to represent sources of attachment. We also expect that photographs taken by local residents will represent a wider range of phenomena than pictures taken by transient visitors.
 
F But how should the photographs be interpreted? Goin (2001) notes that with every photo taken 'a fiction is created … but presents to the uninformed an overwhelming conviction of fact' (p. 363). By implication, what photos appear to be and what they really represent may be very different things, and some follow-up helps to uncover the intended meanings of the participant. Yamashita (2002) notes the utility of asking respondents to provide descriptions of each photo in a notebook or diary. These elaborations are helpful, but in cases of complex phenomena, an interview may help participants clarify their intentions (Markwell, 1997).

Q27

干扰 “Innovation” 对应 “New approach”。A段重点在引出新方法 VEP。

句子 (Paragraph A) “...Visitor Employed Photography (VEP)... represents a potential innovation in sense-of-place research.”

解析 题目对应A段。A段主要介绍了一种新的研究方法“Visitor Employed Photography (VEP)”，并指出它代表了“sense-of-place research（地方感研究）”中的“potential innovation（潜在创新）”，这对应标题 v “地方感研究的新方法”。

Q28

解析 题目对应B段。B段开头就定义了“place（地点）”是一个我们赋予意义的设置，接着讨论了“symbolic 'meanings'（象征意义）”的重要性以及意义如何形成（个体 vs 群体），这对应标题 vi “定义地点的意义”。

干扰 “Defining the significance” 对应原文对 “meaning” 的反复探讨（symbolic meanings, attribute meaning）。

句子 (Paragraph B) “A 'place' is a setting that we give meaning to... Symbolic meanings are important...”

Q29

解析 题目对应C段。C段讨论了地方依恋（place attachment）是通过“familiarity... over a period of months or even years（数月甚至数年的熟悉）”建立的，对比了长期居住（extended residence）和快速产生依恋（develop quite rapidly）的情况，核心是“时间”与“归属感/依恋”的关系，对应标题 i。

干扰 “Relevance of time” 对应 “period of months or years / accumulation of events / rapidly”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “Clearly, place attachment is built through familiarity... over a period of months or even years.”

Q30

句子 (Paragraph D) “Haywood (1990) describes several benefits of VEP... helps to sharpen observation...”

解析 题目对应D段。D段引用Haywood的话，列举了VEP的“several benefits（几个好处）”，如增加乐趣、通过拍照锐化观察（sharpen observation）、便于比较等，这对应标题 iii “摄影在地方感研究中的优势”。

干扰 “Advantages” 对应 “benefits”。

Q31

解析 题目对应E段。E段开头转折“However, several methodological issues need to be taken into account（然而，几个方法论问题需要被考虑）”，接着讨论了谁来拍照、拍照时间限制等潜在陷阱，这对应标题 vii “使用VEP时的重要考虑因素”。

干扰 “Important considerations” 对应 “issues need to be taken into account”。

句子 (Paragraph E) “However, several methodological issues need to be taken into account.”

Q32

解析 题目对应F段。F段首句提出问题“But how should the photographs be interpreted?（但照片应该如何被解读？）”，接着讨论照片可能创造虚构，需要访谈或日记来澄清意图，这正是关于如何理解/解读摄影研究，对应标题 ii “理解摄影研究”。

干扰 “Making sense of” 对应 “interpreted / uncover meanings”。

句子 (Paragraph F) “But how should the photographs be interpreted?”

Q33

解析 题目说我们对某地的依恋可以很快发生。原文C段 Tuan 指出在“chosen places（选择的地方）”，依恋可能“develop quite rapidly（相当迅速地发展）”，即很快发生，选 D。

干扰 “Happen quickly” 对应 “develop quite rapidly / immediate attachment”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...Tuan (1977) notes that a sense of place may also develop quite rapidly...”

Q34

干扰 “Limiting the amount of time” 对应 “compressing the photo-taking period into a single day”。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...Haywood (1990) suggests that compressing the photo-taking period... may result in an over-representation...”

解析 题目说限制拍照时间可能会产生狭窄的图像范围。原文E段 Haywood 建议说将拍照时间压缩到“single day（单日）”可能导致“over-representation of tourist icons（旅游标志的过度表现/范围狭窄）”，而不是普通地方，选 E。

Q35

解析 题目说一个群体的成员会对某个地方持有相似的观点。原文B段 Greider & Garkovich 断言意义基于社会类别，因此在这些类别内部是“shared by others（被其他人共享的/相似的）”，例如农民对土地的看法，选 B。

干扰 “Members of a group... similar view” 对应 “shared by others within these categories”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “Others, however, (e.g. Greider & Garkovich, 1994) assert that meanings... are shared by others within these categories.”

Q36

解析 题目说假以时日，一个地方对我们的影响可以像人（家人）一样。原文C段 Ryden 指出长期居住（Extended residence）让我们对地方的感觉就像对待一个活物（living thing），影响我们的情感“in the same way as a family would（就像家庭一样）”，选 C。

干扰 “Same impact... as people do” 对应 “same way as a family would”。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...affecting our emotions in the same way as a family would (Ryden, 1993).”

Q37

句子 (Paragraph F) “Yamashita (2002) notes the utility of asking respondents to provide descriptions... in a notebook or diary.”

解析 题目说游客应该对他们的照片做书面记录。原文F段 Yamashita 指出要求受访者在笔记本或日记中提供每张照片的“descriptions（描述/书面记录）”是有用的，选 G。

干扰 “Written account” 对应 “descriptions... in a notebook or diary”。

Q38

解析 题目说每个地方对每个游客意味着不同的东西。原文B段 Meinig 建议因为意义源于个人经历，所以“place meanings are completely individualistic（地点意义完全是个人主义的）”，有多少人就有多少种意义，选 A。

干扰 “Means something different to each” 对应 “contain as many different meanings as there are people”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...place meanings are completely individualistic... (Meinig, 1979).”

Q39

解析 题目问Yamashita在2002年的研究表明当地居民____。原文E段提到Yamashita指出居民可能比游客更难表达视觉吸引力，正是因为他们是“insiders（内部人员/太熟悉）”并且“less conscious of aesthetic qualities（对美学品质意识较少/难以欣赏）”，对应选项 B (know their surroundings too well to appreciate them)。

干扰 A（欣赏美）与原文 “difficulty expressing / less conscious” 相反；C（水最重要）原文只说关注水质，未说最重要；D（不喜欢游客影响）未提及。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...precisely because they are insiders and less conscious of aesthetic qualities.”

Q40

解析 题目问在最后一段作者认为照片呈现的是____。原文F段引用Goin说照片创造了“fiction（虚构）”，表面呈现的和实际代表的可能非常不同，因此需要后续采访来“clarify their intentions（澄清他们的意图/解释）”，对应选项 D (an image that needs to be explained to others)。

干扰 A（事实记录）被 “fiction is created” 否定；B（不可靠来源）太绝对，作者认为需要辅助解释而非完全不可靠；C（清晰感受）被 “what they really represent may be very different” 否定。

句子 (Paragraph F) “...what photos appear to be and what they really represent may be very different... interview may help participants clarify their intentions.”
